text:
morgan: Hey, CI red on the canary publish — image push failed in job `build-image-4523` when uploading a layer. Logs show 403/permission denied for one blob. anyone seen this pattern?

raj: throwing the log here: 
```
[upload 1/6] Pushing layer sha256:abcd...
error: unexpected status: 403 Forbidden
server: "unauthorized: uploading blob is not permitted by ACL"
```

lina: hmm, we rotated the gov-cloud registry token last night. did the bastion creds get updated in the builder agents? :thinking:

morgan: i checked — token was rotated but the deploy key was updated only for the runner pool, not the ephemeral builders. CI uses the ephemeral pool for canaries.

sam: do we know which layer failed? root vs app layer? sometimes a `COPY --chown=` change causes uid shift and troubles with kaniko caching.

morgan: output shows it failed on layer 4 (app code layer). Dockerfile recently changed: added `COPY --chown=1001:1001 . /app` in PR #7842. CI job had been green before that.

raj: two possible problems: (1) auth token for builder cannot write that blob (403) OR (2) blob already exists but cache metadata mismatch -> registry rejects finalize. we should try a rerun with fresh cache and with the updated token on builders.

ci-bot: CI status — build-image-4523 failed at 2026-03-17T15:03:22Z (exit code 1). Rerun link: https://ci.redwood/internal/job/4523/rerun

lina: @raj can you flip the builder pool creds? I can do a quick rerun after.

raj: on it. quick check: `kubectl -n ci set secret builder-creds --from-literal=token=<redacted>` then rolling restart of builder job controllers. will push fix in 5m.

morgan: thanks. also while we're at it, can we disable kaniko cache for this run? suspected cache corruption: earlier we saw `blob size mismatch` on a different registry and disabling cache forced a fresh upload which succeeded.

sam: +1 for no-cache. command for our runner: `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 kaniko --no-cache ...` (or the CI flag `image.cache: false`).

raj: creds updated and builder pods restarted. triggered a rerun with cache disabled: job 4523-rerun-1.

ops-bot: deploy note: registry token rotation detected. If unauthorized persists, rotate KMS keys for builder service account.

morgan: rerun started — watch logs at https://ci.redwood/internal/job/4523-rerun-1

(5m later)

morgan: rerun failed again but different error now: `manifest finalize: 409 Conflict: layer digest mismatch` — looks like cache or compression variant issue. log: 
```
Uploading layer sha256:abcd... size=3.2MiB
manifest finalize failed: 409 Conflict (digest mismatch)
registry: existing blob has different digest for same content length
```

lina: that smells like corruption on the registry side or ZSTD vs gzip compression difference. Did buildx or kaniko change compression flags?

sam: our recent Dockerfile added `RUN npm ci --production` which changed tar ordering a bit (mtime differences). Normally buildkit normalizes metadata but kaniko sometimes doesn't. can we force `--compress` or align builder version?

raj: let's try a bisect: create a minimal job that builds only the changed layer and pushes to a staging repo. if staging push fails, it's local to build; if succeeds, registry may be flaky. who can spin that up?

morgan: I can. spinning minimal job `build-minimal-4523-check`. will build with buildkit v0.11 and kaniko v1.9 variants, and with both gzip and zstd. will report back.

ci-bot: queued build-minimal-4523-check. link: https://ci.redwood/internal/job/4523-minimal

(20m later)

morgan: results: 
- buildkit + gzip -> push OK
- kaniko + gzip -> push OK
- kaniko + zstd -> push FAIL (digest mismatch)

morgan: this suggests registry or kaniko+zstd path is producing non-deterministic digest handling.

raj: good find. workaround: disable zstd compression on kaniko runners for now. i'll add a temporary CI config override: set `IMAGE_COMPRESSION=gzip` for the builder pool and redeploy.

lina: can we also add a quick regression test to reproduce the mismatch in CI (small tarball push) so we catch later?

sam: create a tiny test job that builds a trivial layer with same flags and asserts pushed digest matches local digest. put it in the canary pipeline.

raj: config change applied. queued a forced rerun of the original full job (4523-rerun-2) with gzip only.

morgan: rerun-2 succeeded! image pushed and manifest finalized. :tada:

lina: nice. next steps: 
- raj: revert token/creds drift fix into infra repo and add automated sync for builder secret on token rotations.
- sam: add compression consistency test to canary CI.
- morgan: open a bug with kaniko maintainers referencing zstd digest mismatch, link logs.

morgan: filing issues now — PRs incoming. thanks all for the quick triage. :heart:

ci-bot: build-image-4523 completed successfully in 00:22:41. artifact: registry.redwood/internal/canary/image:pr-7842

ops-bot: note: monitoring alert suppressed for registry 403 noise during incident window.

sam: logging action items in the infra board. ping me if you want to pair on the kaniko test.

lina: closing loop. great fast triage.
